newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan one-month CD rate 0.55%, highest since May.
newsitem.headline: Japan one-month CD rate 0.55%, highest since May.

text.p: One-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.55 percent in mid-afternoon on Thursday, the highest rate since May 15, 1996, traders said.

The one-month CDs issued on Thursday are settled on March 3 and mature on April 2, the first such CDs to cover end-of-March book closings, traders said. The issued volume was a small 10 billion yen so far, they said.
The rise in the CD rate from its last issued rate of 0.52 percent reflected commercial banks' strong fund raising demand ahead of the end of the current fiscal year, traders said.
Neither two- nor three-month CDs were issued on Thursday, but they were both offered at 0.54 percent, unchanged from previously issued levels.

Given a widespread view that the Bank of Japan will keep the key overnight call rate from rising above 0.50 percent in the near future, commercial banks prefered to raise funds at the short-end of the market.
This put upward pressure on the key overnight call rate and at the same time resulted in sluggish trade in the long-term CD market, traders said.

The key overnight call rate was mainly traded at 0.53 percent on Thursday, the highest level since April 3, 1996. Wednesday's weighted average rate was 0.51 percent. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8570
